key_insight: The paper proves that the dimension of a simple connected GHZ graph is bounded purely by graph connectivity, specifically by at most 2^(κ(G)-1) + C(κ(G),2).
engineering_relevance: This gives a structural upper limit on how large multipartite GHZ states can be in photonic graph-based constructions, helping researchers assess feasibility before experiment design.
method: Relate GHZ-state dimension to feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colorings of edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs.
Derive a general upper bound in terms of vertex connectivity κ(G) for all simple connected GHZ graphs with at least four vertices.
Extend the analysis with additional bounds based on edge connectivity and maximum degree.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new theoretical bound that generalizes prior results for connectivity at most 2 and improves understanding of GHZ-graph limitations.
watch_item: The bound is structural and theoretical, so experimental realizability still depends on the specific photonic setup and graph encoding details.
